title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 667–669 of the manuscript, Grothendieck's own numbering 537). The notes study profinite groups modelled on the 'universal case' G^+ = GL(2,Z)^ (profinite completion), with G^♮ = Π_0 (a fundamental-group-like normal subgroup). Here G^+, G^♮ are written as fraktur 𝔊^+, 𝔊^♮. Z_{ρ,σ} is the analogue of the normalizer of a cusp inertia subgroup. It sits in an extension 1 → L_0^♮ → Z_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1. L_0^♮ is the closed procyclic group generated by the 'unipotent' g_0, the analogue of (1 1; 0 1). γ_{ρ,σ} is the 'Galois/cyclotomic' quotient, with character χ_σ : γ_{ρ,σ} → Ẑ^×. The previous page found that Z_{ρ,σ} is 'too big' to produce the right analogue G^♮_{ρ,σ} of M_0^! = M(0)·Π_0. So Grothendieck wants a subgroup Z_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ Z_{ρ,σ} playing the role of M(0). It should give a semidirect decomposition Z_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·L_0^♮, and hence G_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·𝔊^+.

(68): Grothendieck then defines (G^♮_{ρ,σ})_0 := Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·𝔊^♮. This lies inside G^♮_{ρ,σ}, which lies inside G_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·𝔊^+. He also sets Z^♮_{ρ,σ} := G^♮_{ρ,σ} ∩ Z_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·(L_0 ∩ 𝔊^♮).

(69)–(72): a standard way to get a canonical splitting of Z_{ρ,σ} → γ_{ρ,σ}.
- Suppose one has a (ρ,σ)-compatible homomorphism 𝔊^+ → PSL(2,Ẑ) = SL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}, equivariant for the action of τ. Think of it as a 'linearization', e.g. the action on the abelianization Ẑ^2 of the π_1 of a once-punctured elliptic curve.
- It induces a map from Z_{ρ,σ} to the 'Borel' group B'_0 = {(μ λ; 0 1)} ≅ Ẑ ⋊ Ẑ^×, the affine group of Ẑ.
- This map sends L_0^♮ to the unipotent radical L'_0 ≅ Ẑ via g_0^n ↦ (1 n; 0 1).
- The result is a morphism of extensions (72): (L_0^♮ → Z → γ) maps to (Ẑ → B'_0 → Ẑ^×), with the right vertical map χ_σ and 'det' (μ,λ) ↦ μ.

If L_0^♮ → Ẑ is an isomorphism, Z_{ρ,σ} is the fibre product B'_0 ×_{Ẑ^×} γ_{ρ,σ}. The diagonal torus T'_0 = {diag(μ,1)} is a splitting of B'_0, so its preimage Z_{ρ,σ}(0) splits Z_{ρ,σ} over γ_{ρ,σ}.

The next page notes that in typical cases (71) is not an isomorphism. Grothendieck then imposes the hypothesis that the preimage of T'_0 is still a section subgroup: it meets L_0^♮ trivially and maps onto γ. He believes this holds 'in all really useful cases' once (69) exists.

In modern terms: one fixes the decomposition group of a tangential base point at a cusp, Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ^×, inside an arithmetic fundamental group. This is done by pulling back the standard torus splitting of the affine group through a linear representation of the geometric part.
errors: Minor notational tension: the target of (69) is SL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}, yet B'_0 has diagonal entry μ ∈ Ẑ^×, so it is not inside PSL(2,Ẑ). It must be read inside the semidirect product with the τ/Galois part, effectively a subgroup of GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}. With the normalization 'lower-right entry 1', det is well defined there. This is implicit, not an error of substance.

The splitting argument is only complete when (71) is an isomorphism, as Grothendieck himself notes on the next page. Otherwise the existence of the section Z_{ρ,σ}(0) is an added hypothesis, supported only by his heuristic belief.

ideas.what: Defining a canonical splitting of the cusp-normalizer extension 1→L_0→Z_{ρ,σ}→γ_{ρ,σ}→1 by pulling back the diagonal torus of the affine group Ẑ⋊Ẑ^× through a τ-equivariant homomorphism to PSL(2,Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: splitting of the decomposition group at a cusp / tangential base point section; Borel subgroup Ẑ(1)⋊Ẑ^× as inertia normalizer
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points); Ihara, Nakamura (cusp decomposition groups in profinite GT/Galois settings)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the Longue Marche as such; the Longue Marche discusses inertia/cusp ('bouts') subgroups and their normalizers in a related spirit

ideas.what: Subgroup (G^♮_{ρ,σ})_0 = Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·𝔊^♮ as analogue of M_0^! = M(0)·Π_0 in the abstract 'loop equation' framework
ideas.modern_name: abstract analogue of the arithmetic fundamental group of a punctured elliptic curve extended by Galois / GT-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (Grothendieck's own framework; GT literature: Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura–Schneps for genus-one variants)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic bookkeeping inside Grothendieck's private axiomatic framework: a fibre-product splitting of an affine-group-type extension. It is natural and in line with standard tangential-base-point and cusp-decomposition-group constructions; nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Top '537' is Grothendieck's own page number (archive page 668).
'scindage de Con. de Z_{ρ,σ}' is better read as 'scindage can.' (canonique) 'de Z_{ρ,σ} sur γ_{ρ,σ}'.
In (68), 'Z^♮_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}' is probably a crossed-out letter: the intended definition is Z^♮_{ρ,σ} = G^♮_{ρ,σ} ∩ Z_{ρ,σ} = Z_{ρ,σ}(0)·(L_0 ∩ 𝔊^♮), with the '||' linking these lines.
In (70), μ ∈ Ẑ^× (units), consistent with det onto Ẑ^× in (72).
